artboards.title: 02.3 · Run diagram (tree view of one run)

annotations.text:
AI Orchestrator v1 — dev-loop screens

Design system: instrument-dark (DESIGN.md 2026-08-25), values lifted verbatim. Colour is signal only: green = running, amber = needs you, red = failed, grey = queued / done.

Status tokens: QUE · RUN · BLK (agent blocked) · CHK (checkpoint) · ERR · DON · SKP.

Static mockups, 1440×900 desktop, one operator. Mock data is illustrative.

Attention rule on every screen

Exactly one thing may be amber or red at a time on a card or row: the reason it needs you. Everything else is grey text. If nothing needs you, the screen has no amber or red pixel.

Words carry the state (blocked, skipped, unvalidated, exit 1) — colour only reinforces.

Board columns are STATUS, not pipeline stage: the v1 template is one dev loop, so the stage lives on the card as 'story 3-2 · build'.

Needs you = BLK + CHK + budget breach. Its header is the only amber label on the page.

Primary reply path is the ANSWER box: the blocked story file is archived to stories/.answers/ with the answer, and the story is re-planned with the answer as prompt context. Harness-independent and survives session loss.

The terminal resume command is the secondary path (Claude / Codex only).
YAML is editable; the diagram is rendered from it and read-only (no drag-and-drop editor — a product in itself, cut for v1). Save creates a new version; running workflows stay pinned.

Run diagram = the Templates renderer with a run's statuses bound. Left-to-right tree: Run → steps → epics (story-id prefix) → stories. One token per node is the only signal; 'now' marks the current node; QUE = scheduled.

No initiative, no cross-repository level: one workflow = one repository (deferred to a future version).
